The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). StackType's only non-presentation readers are GetTypeForAmount (PowerModel.cs:462) and InvokePowerModified's VFX split (Creature.cs:628). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterApplied.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The skip condition is `base.Owner.IsEnemy` and nothing else. RitualPower.cs:36-43's `AfterApplied` sets WasJustAppliedByEnemy from the OWNER's side and never consults the applier; the port tested `applier is not None and applier.side != owner.side`, which is False exactly where C#'s is True, because every ported Ritual source is a MONSTER buffing ITSELF. powers.py's RitualPower now reads `self._was_just_applied = (owner.side == 'enemy')`. The player-side direction is unchanged in both models. EXECUTED: the Calcified/Damp Cultist pair ends turn 1 at Strength 0/0 where it used to be 2/5, so the whole ladder shifts a turn later and the turn-2 strikes land unbuffed (player 80 -> 70, not 80 -> 63). THREE LEGACY TESTS MOVED (non-negotiable 5), each with the reason inline: test_powers.py's `test_skips_first_trigger_when_applied_by_enemy` / `test_does_not_skip_when_applied_by_self` were an applier-side pair and are now an OWNER-side pair on a plain monster; test_underdocks.py's `test_incantation_then_scaling_strikes` and test_glory.py's `test_incantation_then_scaling_savage` (Devoted Sculptor, the biggest Ritual in the game at 9) both gained the extra turn. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: LIVE. The skip-first-trigger condition is wrong. RitualPower.cs:36-43 sets `WasJustAppliedByEnemy = true` whenever **base.Owner.IsEnemy** -- the applier is not consulted at all. powers.py:194-196 instead sets it when `applier is not None and applier.side != owner.side`. Every ported Ritual source is a MONSTER buffing ITSELF, so the sim's test is False exactly where C#'s is True and the enemy gets one extra Strength application, on the very turn it casts Ritual. EXECUTED with the ported Calcified Cultist (monsters/underdocks/cultists.py:39, `applier=self`): after one round the sim shows Strength(2) and Ritual(2), where the game skips that first AfterSideTurnEnd and shows no Strength at all. Damp Cultist (Ritual 5) and Devoted Sculptor (monsters/glory/devoted_sculptor.py:42) are the same shape, so the error scales with the biggest Ritual in the game. The player-side direction is unaffected: with a player owner C#'s Owner.IsEnemy is false and the sim's applier-side test is also false, so both trigger on the first turn end. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE PLAYER LEG IS CLOSED: it is now `after_player_turn_end` (powers.py:236-238), the sim's Hook.AfterTurnEnd slot (combat.py:809 / CombatManager.cs:1307). WHAT REMAINS is the ENEMY leg: powers.py:232-234 is still the per-creature `on_enemy_turn_end`, which runs right after THIS enemy's move, where Hook.AfterTurnEnd runs once at CombatManager.cs:1256 after every enemy has moved. `on_enemy_side_end` is the right slot and this power still does not use it. Cross-referenced to turn_structure G5, as the guard entry records.

guards.rationale: powers.py:199-201 clears the flag and returns on the first trigger, so the skip is once-only on both sides. The BUG is which applications set the flag, not how it is consumed -- see the AfterApplied entry.

powers.py:202-203 routes through StrengthCmd.apply (cmds.py:349-361) instead, which first runs hooks.modify_strength_given and then calls PowerCmd.apply with NO applier. Two differences with the same observable today: the extra modify_strength_given chain has no C# analogue at this site, and dropping `applier = Owner` means a Ritual-granted Strength is applier-less. Neither is observable now -- an executed grep finds no ported modify_strength_given listener that fires for an enemy target, and no ported effect keys on a Strength application's applier for an enemy owner. Kept as a divergence rather than faithful because the applier is exactly what PossessStrengthPower (powers.py:3092-3099) tracks, so a monster holding both Ritual and Possess Strength would expose it.
